At 14 months of age, the patient had a weight of 8.6 kg (under the 15th percentile), a length of 74 cm (under the 10th percentile), and his vital signs were within normal ranges. Physical examination revealed macrocephaly, nystagmus (visual disturbance), the aforementioned cranial characteristics along with thick lips, epicanthal folds, large pinnae, thick eyebrows, dental malocclusion, and strabismus (Fig. 2A and C).Fig. 2Photograph of the patient showing facial appearance of Costello syndrome. The musculoskeletal evaluation revealed a short neck, hypotonia, increased anteroposterior chest diameter, broad distal phalanges, ulnar deviation of the hands (Fig. 2B), and pectus carinatum. Skin assessment based on epithelial alterations revealed loose skin of the hands and feet, curly hair, and deep palmar and plantar folds.
